record.original_question: Let p be a prime, let C be a nonzero element of the finite field F(p), and let alpha be a primitive root modulo p. Determine the number of integers i in [p-1] that satisfy the congruence i ≡ C alpha^i (mod p).

evidence.quote: Problem 19. Let p be a prime, C ∈ F* (p), and α a primitive root of F(p). Determine the number of roots i ∈ [p − 1] of i ≡ Cαi mod p.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $\mathbb{F}_p$ denote the finite field with $p$ elements, let $C \in \mathbb{F}_p^{*}$ be a nonzero element, and let $\alpha$ be a primitive root modulo $p$ (i.e., a generator of the cyclic group $\mathbb{F}_p^{*}$). Consider the congruence
$$ i \equiv C\,\alpha^{i} \pmod{p}. $$
Determine, as a closed-form expression (or sharp asymptotic / exact formula) in terms of $p$, $C$, and $\alpha$, the number of integers $i \in \{1, 2, \dots, p-1\}$ that satisfy this congruence.
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in a 2011 collection of open problems on Costas arrays (where it concerns fixed points of Welch-construction W1 arrays). No subsequent literature found resolving the count of solutions to i ≡ Cα^i (mod p) in closed form; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among open problems in Costas arrays with no resolution cited.
